title: Length bound for encoded call words
statement: Let $m,d$ be nonnegative integers, let $\Lambda$ be a type, and let a call specification have at most $m$ registers, select a decider among $d$ choices, choose a mode and an ordered list of registers, and specify successor states for positive and negative answers. For an input bit string $x$, assign each register $r$ a bit string $V(r)$, and suppose every assigned string has length at most $W$ and the selected register list contains no repetitions. Then the virtual call word formed from the mode-dependent first segment, the selected register strings (with the prescribed doubling), and separators has length at most $2|x|+2+m(2W+2)$, where $|x|$ denotes the length of $x$.
